Viktranium Experiment crafting is a Heroic (ML 8) and Legendary (ML34) crafting system introduced in Update 75: The Chill of Ravenloft.

The system is very similar to Dinosaur Bone crafting: Collect ingredients, craft them into specially typed Lamordia augments, and place those augments into special augment slots.

Ingredients[edit]

This crafting system features a total of 7 crafting ingredients, which come in Heroic and Legendary versions:

Found in Chill of Ravenloft quests, wilderness encounters and raid. These ingredients are Unbound:
(Legendary) Bleak Conductors
(Legendary) Bleak Insulators
(Legendary) Bleak Alternators
(Legendary) Bleak Resistors
Found in the raid and wilderness encounters. These ingredients are Unbound:
(Legendary) Bleak Wires
Found in the raid and special wilderness encounters. These ingredients are Bound to Account on Acquire:
(Legendary) Bleak Transformers
Found in the raid only, existing only as a Legendary version. These ingredients are Bound to Account on Acquire:
Legendary Bleak Mementos
Crafting[edit]

Interact with the workbenches in Ludendorf City Hall (one workbench each for the Heroic and Legendary systems) to access the barter window to create Lamordia augments and Calamitous weapons. To slot a Lamordia augment into a Lamordia augment slot, use the Augment Item UI accessible through your Inventory Panel.

Heroic Calamitous weapons cost 5 Bleak Alternators, 5 Bleak Conductors, 5 Bleak Insulators and 5 Bleak Resistors to craft and cannot have Mythic bonuses.

Heroic Calamitous weapons have:
Minimum Level 8
+4 Enhancement Bonus and 1[W].
Vampirism 1
Melancholic Slot (Weapon)
Dolorous Slot (Weapon)
Miserable Slot (Weapon)
Red Augment Slot
These items are Bound to Account on Acquire

Legendary Calamitous weapons cost 25 Legendary Bleak Alternators, 25 Legendary Bleak Conductors, 25 Legendary Bleak Insulators and 25 Legendary Bleak Resistors to craft and cannot have Mythic bonuses.

Legendary Calamitous weapons have:
Minimum Level 34
+15 Enhancement Bonus, 5.8[W], and +2/+4 loaded weapon dice (For 1h and 2h weapons respectively)
Melancholic Slot (Weapon)
Dolorous Slot (Weapon)
Miserable Slot (Weapon)
Woeful Slot (Weapon)
Orange Augment Slot
Purple Augment Slot
These items are Bound to Account on Acquire

A full list of craftable (Heroic and Legendary) Calamitous weapons can be seen here: Calamitous weapons

Legendary Cataclysmic weapons cost the same amount of regular materials as Legendary Calamitous weapons, but additionally require 25 Legendary Bleak Mementos, a material only dropped in the raid Relentless.

These items are Bound to Character on Acquire
Information about them can be found here, in the section regarding the raid. They are crafted inside of the raid, using a special crafting station.
Crafting can be done before the raid begins, safely and without activating any hostile monsters.
Unlike Calamitous, it is possible to craft Cataclysmic shields. These shields cost the same materials as any other Cataclysmic weapon.
A full list of craftable Cataclysmic weapons and shields can be seen here: Cataclysmic weapons and shields
The only real difference between Legendary Calamitous and Cataclysmic weapons (of the same type) is that Cataclysmic weapons have +3/+6 loaded weapon dice.
Due to possessing no other changes compared to Calamitous weapons, there is no reason to craft a Cataclysmic weapon for casters. Cataclysmic weapons possess the same slots and lack any further bonuses, while being Bound to Character on Acquire and thus harder to store.
Lamordia Augments[edit]

There are 4 Lamordia augment types, each requiring ingredients from different locations (the Set Bonus slot found on Dinosaur Bone items is here replaced by Sun and Moon Augment Slots):

Melancholic (Quests)
Dolorous (Quests)
Miserable (Wilderness)
Woeful (Raid or special Wilderness encounters)

These augment types can come in multiple variants: Armor, Weapon, and Accessory. Each augment type can only fit into an augment slot that exactly matches its type. For example, a "Melancholic (Weapon)" augment cannot go in a "Melancholic Slot (Armor)" slot, only a "Melancholic Slot (Weapon)" slot. You can check which augment type an augment is by looking at its tooltip for the Augment Type row, and then match it to the tooltip of the item you are trying to augment.

Note that Heroic slots will accept Legendary augments (and vice versa) but a Legendary augment will increase the minimum level of a heroic item to 34.

Items with Lamordia augment slots[edit]
C:Viktranium Experiment Crafting items
Most standard named items from The Chill of Ravenloft have a Melancholic and Dolorous Lamordia augment slot. Certain items (including Rare items and Minor Artifacts) additionally have a Miserable Slot. Calamitous Weapons have all three slots, plus a Woeful slot on Legendary only. Downcast Armor items are the only items to possess a Woeful (Accessory) slot.

Wicked Viktranium Experiment Crafting[edit]

Crafting Device
Device location in the raid entrance

Wicked Viktranium Experiment Crafting is a separate crafting machine that creates extra augment options using the standard Legendary Viktranium Experiment ingredients and Bleak Mementos, a unique ingredient from the legendary raid Relentless. Only Legendary versions of these augments are available.

The device is found inside the raid Relentless, where it is located at the beginning and can be accessed before the wax statues activate. Find it to the left, through the door, when you enter. (The device can also be accessed at the corresponding location in the Ludendorf Wax Museum in the Lamordia wilderness.)

BUG': Currently you cannot click on the doors in the Wax Museum to open. To open, you must use the keyboard - target the doors with the target key, then press the interact key.

Unslotting[edit]

Lamordia augments can be unslotted or overwritten:

You can destroy a currently-slotted augment by placing a new augment into the slot.
You can unslot a Lamordia augment by using a Viktranium Pick, which is a rare ingredient found within chests in the Chill of Ravenloft pack or purchased in the DDO Store. This process returns the augment to you unharmed so that you may slot it in a new location. Viktranium Picks may also be found as rewards from Chill of Ravenloft's Sagas. A Jeweler's Tool Kit will not work.

text:
Fortification represents a percentage chance to negate additional damage incurred from a critical hit or sneak attack.

When a critical hit is negated, damage is applied normally rather than at the critical hit multiplier.
Weapon enchantments that trigger on a critical hit (e.g. Holy Burst, Bloodletter or Radiance) continue to work even if the critical hit itself is negated.
When a sneak attack is negated, the extra damage is not applied.

In DDO, most players strive for roughly +10% fortification per level, with the most durable characters achieving +300% at level 30. Most monsters don't have fortification, unless it is granted by the race/type (e.g. Undead, Constructs). Quest and raid bosses have higher fortification, but usually not full.

Players and monsters can gain abilities to bypass a portion of fortification.

Sources of Fortification[edit]

Items are the primary source of fortification for most player characters. Standard fortification items provide enhancement bonuses to fortification. Multiple effects do not stack with each other. You can combine them with rarer Insightful Fortification items (insight bonus). Item effects fully stack with the racial fortification, enhancements, or epic destiny perks.

Penalty to fortification[edit]

Some effects reduce your fortification:

Yugoloth Essence of Cunning potion
Improved Sunder
Various monster only special attacks, such as Bebilith's Rend Armor
Fortification on Monsters[edit]
Any monster that belongs to a type or race that are considered "immune to critical hits" (Undead, Oozes, Constructs and Elementals) gains a natural Fortification of 100%. This also applies to summoned creatures and pets.
Multiple Monster Champion types gain bonuses to Fortification depending on their Tier.
Some monsters also gain buffs to Fortification on a quest-specific basis. Most quest and raid bosses have at least some fortification, with legendary raid bosses almost always having over 100%. Monsters can also gain fortification buffs from certain quest mechanics.
Bypassing Fortification[edit]

Since Update 13, monsters with sneak attack dice are able to bypass some of the player fortification equal to monsters' Challenge Rating. (DDO Forums 

UPDATE ME!

) E.g.:

If a CR 1 Kobold Sneak attacks someone with 50% fortification, the Kobold Sneak has a 51% chance to normally conduct a critical hit or sneak attack.
If a CR 20 Lava Mephit attacks someone with 100% fortification, the Lava Mephit has a 20% chance to normally conduct a critical hit or sneak attack.
If a CR 54 Sellsword Footpad attacks someone with 150% fortification, the Sellsword Footpad has a 4% chance to normally conduct a critical hit or sneak attack.
If a CR 29 Earth Elemental attacks someone with 125% fortification, it is still going to have a 0% chance to critically hit or sneak attack, as it has no sneak attack dice.

Players can bypass a portion of enemy fortification (personal benefit), or generally reduce enemy fortification (universal benefit).

Bypassing immunity to sneak attack[edit]

In addition to fortification, monsters can possess "sneak attack immunity" that prevents sneak attacks (even at 100% fort bypass). Some special effects can remove that immunity. (Originally from DDO Vault)

Assassin's Trick
Wracking Shot
Shadowdancer capstone
Smoke Trap: they lose their immunity to sneak attack...
